entities.name: The Consul
entities.description:
The Consul was a mentor to the Dominus of the Cabal Empire, Ghaul.

Long before the events of Destiny 2, the Consul advised Ghaul in his successful military coup against the previous Cabal emperor, Calus.

At some point in his lifetime, the Cabal Emperor Calus rose to power. Calus' first move as emperor was to exile the Consul, leading him to form a strong hate for the Cabal Emperor. This hate then became the foundation for gathering members including Ghaul and overthrowing Emperor Calus.

Following Ghaul's conquering of the Last City, the Consul became increasingly frustrated with Ghaul for his continued inquiries with the Speaker as to how he might earn the Light instead of taking it by force. These feelings only increased when the cage was completed and Ghaul still refused to simply steal the Light. The Consul's frustration finally turned to anger when the lone Guardian succeeded in destroying the Almighty and the Vanguard began their attack on the Red Legion in the City. Seeing all they had worked for crumbling because of Ghaul's stubborn refusal to steal the Light, he confronted his student. When Ghaul's response was to consult the Speaker one last time, the Consul released the Speaker from his bonds, furiously berated Ghaul, and crushed the Speaker's mask when he noticed Ghaul staring at it. Angered by his insolence and hostility, Ghaul grabbed the Consul by the throat and assured him that he would take the Light as he choked his old mentor to death.

He took his legion and went to conquer the Reef, but was defeated by the Reef forces and later thrown into the Prison of Elders.

She utilized cloaking technology and traps in battle. She was imprisoned in the Prison of Elders alongside the other Scorn Barons before being set free by Uldren Sov.

Little is known about the exploits of Araskes before the events of the Red War. She is notorious for creating tall tales and legends of her exploits that are not true or filled with inaccuracies.

Araskes appears as a target in the quest Target: The Trickster. She utilizes Web Mines in battle.

True to her nature, Araskes engages in little direct combat, preferring to use her smoke dash ability to escape trouble.

entities.name: Atraks-1
entities.description:
Atraks-1 was a Eliksni exo and a member of House Salvation's Dark council.

Following the collapse of Riis from the Whirlwind, the Eliksni left their homeworld and sought salvation by desperately chasing the Great Machine through space for centuries. During the Long Drift, the Eliksni raised their clans and offspring in their starships and turned them into family homes. Atraks was among a new generation of Eliksni that were born in space and regarded to be unlucky as they had no memories of Riis apart from knowledge retold in stories.Clarity Control breached. A single unregistered Exo and a single life form of unknown biology detected in the Crypt laboratory.

As a fireteam of Guardians entered the Clovis Bray laboratory near Clarity Control, they encountered Atraks near a terminal with the appearance of an Exo and modelled after her previous Eliksni form with four arms and a signature white and black look. She then unleashed the body from the cryopod to reveal the infamous mercenary, Taniks, the Scarred. Taniks was enraged at the sight of the Guardians and proceeded to violently bash the laboratory glass. His attempt to break the glass ended with failure and he then decided to climb the glass and leave Atraks behind. The Fallen Exo also followed suit and disappeared in a mist.

As the Guardians approached the laboratory launch pods, Atraks returned and spread duplicate clones of herself across the room and the Morning Star orbital station to battle against them. She then summoned Fallen reinforcements and deployed Sentinel Servitors to disable the augment terminals nearby. Immune to all damage and armed with an upgraded white Shock Rifle, she fired Arc bullets against them from all directions.

In one of the more important events of the war, she slaughtered the population of Amethyst, a Reef settlement, in order to trick the Queen's Armada into fighting Parixas, one of Skolas' rivals for Kellship. Elykris is notorious for her previous raids on ships and settlements in the Mars region. She took part in the siege of Arran along with the heists after the Solis Descent. She was imprisoned in the Prison of Elders alongside the other Scorned Barons, before they were freed. Elykris then proceded to run rampant across the Tangled Shore, before she was killed by The Guardian, only later to be revived for the heroic ether harvest public event, suggesting that she still remains an active threat alongside the Fanatic.

Elykris appears in Target: The Machinist.

Elykris possesses multiple weapons in her arsenal, all of which have devastating consequences. In hand, she wields a [https://www.destinypedia.com/index.php?title=Scorn_Cannon&action=edit&redlink=1 Scorn Cannon], which fires explosive [https://www.destinypedia.com/Ether Ether] fumes from long range, constantly blasting the player down and pounding away at their shield.

entities.description:
Eramis, Kell of Darkness (formerly the Shipstealer) was the Kell of the House of Salvation, and former baroness of the Fallen House of Devils. She is the main antagonist of Beyond Light.

Eramis was a member of the House of Dancers, eventually joining the House of Devils after the "Long Drift". After the events of the Red War and the House of Devils broken, she discovered a lost SIVA weapon, Outbreak Perfected, with the help of Mithrax, before he defected and formed the House of Light. Later when Mithrax helped the Guardian find the location of the rifle and claim it, she went to Europa, a moon on Jupiter that was long abandoned in hopes to rebuild the Eliksni empire without the Vanguard finding them.

Eramis formed a council on Europa and learned the power of Stasis.

Eramis is very harsh, impatient, and naive. She is always in need of guidance mainly from Kridis, the Dark Priestess, she is also very cowardly, this is shown from her reactivating an old Vex portal made by Clovis Bray-I. She has a deep hatred towards The Traveler and the Guardian.
entities.short_description: Eramis, Kell of Darkness (formerly the Shipstealer) was the Kell of the House of Salvation, and former baroness of the Fallen House of Devils. She is the main antagonist of Beyond Light.

entities.name: Fikrul
entities.description:
Fikrul, the Fanatic is the Archon of the Scorn, a race of undead Eliksni, and the leader of its Barons. He calls Uldren Sov father, likely believing him to be the source of his power. Due to his resurrection ability, Fikrul can seemingly never truly be killed, and has retorted that he will continue to return to seek vengeance upon the Guardian.

Fikrul was once a well-regarded Archon Priest, serving Kaliks Prime, and was a friend of Variks. But he was rejected and cast out after speaking out against The Great Machine. Joining the outcast Barons, he preached the idea that the Eliksni must be wiped out so that they may rise stronger.

He and the other seven Scorn barons were eventually captured. Fikrul managed to escape, but was gravely wounded in the process. Uldren Sov found him, and indirectly wished to Riven, an Ahamkara, to save him. Riven healed Fikrul, giving him the power to resurrect dead Fallen into Scorn. He then went with Uldren to take over the Fallen House of Kings, which they succeeded in doing. They then parted ways, but they were both eventually captured and imprisoned in the Prison of Elders. Uldren persuaded Variks, the Loyal to release himself and the Scorned Barons out from the prison, and they proceeded to run rampant on the Tangled Shore, until they were stopped by the Guardian. Later, after the Coalition defeated The Witness, he would claim the Echo of Riis, one of the Echoes that were created following the Witness’s defeat.

Fikrul is often fueled by rage and a loyalty to Uldren Sov.

entities.name: Grayor
entities.description:
Grayor, Wolf Assassin is an Eliksni Vandal Major of the House of Wolves who could be found in the Mothyards, Old Russia, Earth. He was the target of a wanted Bounty for The Queen's Wrath.

During the Reef Wars, Grayor was one of Skolas' most loyal servants. He worked closely with Drevis and her Silent Fang.

At some point after the death of Irxis, Grayor and Drevis launched two seperate attacks, Drevis slaughtering the population at the Reef settlement of Amethyst, and Grayor assaulting Parixas' Ketch. Both of these attacks were part of a plan to lure the Queen's Armada to Iris, where Parixas had also been lured to, so that Skolas' rival could be killed.

The plan worked, and in fury over the losses on Amethyst, Paladin Abra Zire attacked Parixas, thinking that she was attacking Drevis. After the battle, Paladin Zire realized her mistake, but it was too late. Grayor and Drevis had already slipped away, while Parixas lay dead.

entities.name: Hiraks
entities.description:
Hiraks, the Mindbender was a Scorn Baron that appears in Destiny 2: Forsaken. Hiraks is an Ascended Eliksni who reigns over his own section of the Ascendant Plane. As such, he had the ability to summon Hive combatants to fight alongside him. He wielded a powerful Boomer in battle. He was imprisoned in the Prison of Elders alongside the other Scorn Barons before being set free by Uldren Sov.

Before ascending to his current form, Hiraks was a Dreg that fell deep into the Hellmouth on the Moon. After witnessing closely the Hive civilization, he reemerged obsessed with the race and spoke incomprehensibly. He began to study the race closely and discovered a method of forming his own throne realm located within the Ascendant Realm. His skills grew in the ability to unravel the minds of his enemies, and by channeling the powers and knowledge of the Hive he gained the ability to lead them.

Hiraks was the mastermind of the Great Crow Heist. During the event, Hiraks trapped and converted Prince Uldren's Crows to sow mistrust between the Reef and Earth. He also had a hand in experiments on Asteroid 128 Nemesis, where his actions resulted in an asteroid shifting between the normal dimension and the Ascendant Realm.

Hiraks appears in the adventure Target: The Mindbender. The mission takes place on the Tangled Shore within the Reef.

entities.description:
Kaniks, the Mad Bomber was a Scorn Baron that appeared in Forsaken. Kaniks was a crazed demolitions expert and often loses himself in the adrenaline of explosive combat. He was imprisoned in the Prison of Elders alongside the other Scorn Barons before being set free by Uldren Sov.

Prior to the events of the Red War, Kaniks was responsible for planting the vast minefield located in pockets of The Reef that have claimed several Awoken lives. He was killed by the player in the mission Target: The Mad Bomber.

Kaniks is the target of the Activity Target: The Mad Bomber. He utilizes Void Grenades in combat.

Kaniks' main explosive weapon of choice is the Scorn Grenade, which he throws at The Guardian to continuously bombard their position, breaking their shields in just a handful of explosions, and not taking much longer to outright kill them afterward.

entities.description:

Mithrax was caught by Sjur Eido at one point, and Sjur was able to talk with him.

Mithrax has assisted in some guardian operations. One such assist is when he helped the Guardian disrupt Eramis, the Shipstealer’s attempt to reclaim SIVA and rebuild the House of Devils.

Sometime later, after the events of Beyond Light, Mithrax came to Europa in hopes to escort Eliksni that resented the House of Salvation's cruelty and violence out of the cold moon. And it was revealed that Mithrax is a Splicer, a type of Eliksni that can make portals to the Vex's realm, and was later contacted by Ikora Rey because the Vex had made a simulation of the sun not shining on Earth come true. Mithrax agreed to this, in return being sheltered in the abandoned blocks in the Last City and will be supplied with essentials by the Vanguard. Unfortunately, the neighboring Vex shot down their Skiff and made it crash into the Asterion Abyss, thankfully all of the Refugees survived and ran into a nearby ice cave after contacting Ikora for help. Later on, Ikora sends the Guardian to help escort Mithrax and the refugees away from the raiders and the Vex. After being helped escorted from the cold moon, the Vanguard welcomed the Eliksni with open arms, but was warned that they will keep an eye on them for any suspicious activity. Lakshmi-2 protested against the Vanguard's decision, stating that she "Saw the City on fire, with the Fallen attacking everyone." This guess has led the guardians, but the Vanguard still allowed them to live in the city. But to make sure they didn't have any ideas, they sent down their most feared enemy to watch over them, Saint-14. They described him as an unkillable, wrathful, merciless monster, to be avoided at all costs. Mithrax had mixed feelings about it, but had no other choice but to let the Titan stalk them.

Naksis wears different colored armor and a different headdress. Naksis is shielded by an electric-blue force field that causes significant resistance for anything except headshots. He wears a cape similar to those worn by Fallen in the House of Winter, despite his status as a member of the Devils.

Naksis is equipped with a powerful plasma/energy based weapon and a teleportation ability that allows him to shift a few meters away instantly.

Despite his shielding, Naksis is vulnerable to headshots. With a heavy weapon and concentrated team effort, Naksis can be defeated in a matter of seconds.

entities.description:
Pirrha was a deadly shot and is responsible for the deaths of several notable fighters, such as Awoken Paladins Tellos Cir, Loris Pol, and Hollis Eso at Pallas Falls. He had a penchant for destroying Ghosts to truly end the life of any lightbearer; one such casualty was the Ghost of Cayde-6, Sundance. He used a bullet from a weapon of sorrow that was meant to be used to kill Cayde but instead killed his Ghost. How he came into possession of one is unknown.

Pirrha is the target of the activity Target: The Rifleman. He can be found in the Hellrise Canyon, where he has set up his camp. He lures travelers into an impenetrable security network before eliminating them from a distance.

Pirrha's main weapon of choice is a Scorn crossbowgun, which fires charged Void arrows from long range that can easily hit their mark; their high damage can crack a Guardian's shield in an instant.

When faced at closer ranges, he will teleport or smoke dash to evade and flank the player, and if cornered, he will stomp the ground to knock them back.

entities.description:
Reksis Vahn, the Hangman was a Scorn Baron that appears in Forsaken. He was a depraved executioner who had a strong hatred for Servitors and their place in Eliksni culture. He utilized a Flame Cauldron in combat similar to other Ravagers of the Scorn. He was imprisoned in the Prison of Elders alongside the other Scorn Barons before being set free by Uldren Sov.

Prior to the events of the Red War, Reksis was responsible for exterminating the last Servitors of the House of Wolves, which led to the ultimate destruction of their house. He is the tallest of the Barons, comparable to a Hive Ogre. He siphons Ether from Servitors and channels it to the other Barons, and as such, has been given the nickname "The Godslayer".

Reksis appears as a target in the activity Target: The Hangman.

When at farther ranges, he will smash his censer on the ground to create a large, wide line of flames which quickly burn away at a Guardian's shield and health, and if at point-blank range, he will slam his censer on the floor, creating a shockwave knocks Guardians around and deals massive damage if it hits directly.

Riksis, Devil Archon was a Archon of the House of Devils. The Guardian faced him during the story mission Restoration.

Riksis was once an Archon of the House of Devils. He would collect the skulls of dead Guardians and likely serve them to his Prime Servitor as offerings. However, after a powerful Guardian and their Ghost returned to collect a Warp Drive they had left behind their newfound jumpship, it was revealed the Drive they were searching for was already in Fallen - and most importantly, Riksis' - hands.

Riksis, along with the rest of the Fallen in Dock 13, was killed; it is said that Riksis' death resulted in great joy in The City at the time where it needed hope the most.

Riksis was much larger than his Fallen brethren, due to his rank as a high Archon Priest. He looked similar to that of most Captains, but lacked a shield, something all Captains share.

entities.name: Skolas
entities.description:
Skolas, Kell of Kells was the self-proclaimed Kell of the House of Wolves who rose to power during the rebellion against Queen Mara Sov of The Reef. He is the boss of the story mission Queen's Ransom and Prison of Elders challenge Skolas's Revenge.

Originally, Skolas was a Captain in the House of Wolves. When the Queen's Harbingers killed Virixas, Kell of Wolves at Ceres, Skolas, along with Parixas and Irxis, entered the race for Kellship. The dispute quickly escalated into civil war, with the three claimants for the title leading their respective sides. Like Parixas, Skolas had the loyalty of the Kaliks Servitors, whereas Irxis held the Orbiks Servitors.

Skolas' forces, led by Peekis, killed Irxis in the Eos Clash. Skolas decided to manipulate the Reef into eliminating Parixas, rather than devote his own forces to the effort and risk heavy casualties. He sent Drevis, Wolf Baroness and the Silent Fang to the Awoken station at Amethyst. Drevis and Grayor, Wolf Assassin then slaughtered the station's inhabitants. They then lured Paladin Abra Zire to Iris, where Zire found a Ketch seemingly undefended. The Paladin's forces destroyed the Ketch, only to learn that it belonged to Parixas and not Drevis. With no opponents left, Skolas crowned himself Kell of Wolves.

Drevis was eventually captured in the Battle of Bamberga's Wrath and brought to the fortress at Pallas. Another of Skolas' lieutenants, Pirsis, amassed "the largest Wolf fleet seen since the Scatter" and besieged Pallas. The battle eventually grew into a stalemate, as neither side could unleash their full might without risking collateral damage.

Spider is the leader of the House of Spider located in the Tangled Shore. Once the Scorn overran the area, he retreated into a hideout and allies himself with The Guardian and Petra Venj to clear the region of Scorn and other escaped Prison of Elders convicts. He serves as the primary vendor of the area, assigning bounties and providing material purchases and exchanges.

As the leader of an Eliksni crime organization, the Spider focuses on smuggling items across the region. The organization was long established in the Tangled Shore prior to the events of Forsaken and the chaos sowed by the Scorn. The Spider is fluent in English, similar to Variks, the Loyal. He prefers to negotiate conflicts rather than partake in violence.

The Spider has a strange fascination with human culture and is often seen toying with the fragments of a dead Ghost. He accepts Ghost Fragments as payment for accepting bounties.

The Spider has a list of Bounties for Guardians to purchase. These high value targets reward Legendary rewards for completion. Each bounty requires a payment of Ghost Fragments to accept. {| class="article-table" border="0" cellspacing="1" cellpadding="1" style="width:600px;"

entities.name: Taniks
entities.description:
Beyond Light|gender=Male}} Taniks, the Scarred, also known as Taniks, the Abomination, Taniks, Reborn or Taniks Perfected was an Eliksni mercenary that can be encountered in certain Strikes and locations.

Taniks was a mercenary among the Fallen and is not directly affiliated with any one House, instead offering his services to the highest bidder. He is responsible for the release of Aksor from the Prison of Elders, as well as the murder of Andal Brask, the Hunter Vanguard preceding Cayde-6.

It is believed by the Fallen that he is undying, a living huntsman whose physical self is joined with a mix of technologies, each pilfered from legendary treasure troves. But treasure is not the only currency of value to Taniks. His true ambitions rest in the challenge of the feats in front of him, and the rewards simply allow him to exist free of any Kell’s rule.

Two years later, during the SIVA Crisis, the Devil Splicers resurrected Taniks using SIVA. Taniks, now Taniks Perfected, and his mercenary crew join the Devil Splicers, once again using his old Ketch as a base of operations. Zavala and Ikora Rey task a Fireteam of Guardians, including the Guardian, with defeating him once again.

entities.name: Variks
entities.description:
Variks, the Loyal is an Eliksni Vandal and the only known surviving member of the House of Judgment. As of Forsaken, Variks has abandoned the Awoken and reformed the House of Judgment with himself as the leader.

Variks served as the House of Judgment envoy to Skolas during the Reef Wars. However, Variks was disturbed by Skolas' brutality, and after Skolas docked him of his upper arms, he abandoned the Kell and joined the Reef. His betrayal allowed the Queen to learn of Skolas' impending attack on Cybele, leading to Skolas' incarceration.

After the House of Wolves rebelled against Queen Mara Sov, he remained loyal.

After the attack on Oryx's Dreadnaught and the disappearance of both Mara and Uldren Sov, Variks became the de facto spymaster and commander of the Reef's intelligence contingency, the Crows. He used them to look for a suitable Fallen worthy of being the Kell of Kells to unite the Fallen.

entities.description:
Ada-1, previously known as Adelaide Meyrin, is an Exo that serves as the current curator of the Black Armory.

Ada-1 was born as Adelaide Meyrin during the height of the Golden Age. She was the daughter of Henriette Meyrin, who was one of the three leaders of the Black Armory. During the events of the Collapse, she was gravely injured and her consciousness was placed into an Exo frame by her mother. The Darkness would go on to kill all of the leaders of the Black Armory.

Ada-1 currently resides as the last gatekeeper to the Black Armory and has an uneasy relationship with Guardians. She reluctantly allows the Guardian into the Black Armory, but only on the condition that they find the Forges that were lost.

Ada-1 is located in the Black Armory, which is located behind a secret door in the Annex of the Tower. Access can be granted into the Armory after talking with The Spider and using the Black Armory Badge.

entities.description:
Banshee-44 is the gunsmith in the Tower and sells weapons, ammo syntheses, and weapon telemetries. Once a Guardian reaches level 38, Banshee-44 will offer field test weapons, which refresh every week on Armsday. Each field test weapon has a unique requirement, such as killing Cabal or achieving precision kills in the Crucible, that may be fulfilled while using the weapon. Once the requirement is fulfilled, the Guardian will immediately gain Gunsmith reputation. The field test weapon can then be dismantled without penalty if the Guardian does not wish to keep it.

Once a Guardian reaches rank 1 in Gunsmith reputation, he or she will be able to order legendary weapons, which arrive and refresh each Armsday. The number of simultaneous orders that can be placed is equal to the Guardian's gunsmith reputation (for example, a Guardian at rank 3 will be able to place three orders). Orders can only be placed Wednesday through Saturday.

Like all Exo, he was originally designed as a war machine. Following reactivation, Banshee-44 made his way to the Last City, setting up a shop selling weapons and ammo synthesis packs to Guardians.

Banshee-44 was Clovis Bray I in his human life, and after defeating most of the Vex invasion on Europa, Clovis-43 decided to erase his identity and start anew, taking on the name Banshee-44.

entities.description:
The Exo Stranger, also known as Elsie Bray, is an Exo who is interested in the Guardian's activities.

In A Guardian Rises, the Exo Stranger appeared observing the reborn Guardian and the Ghost's escape from Old Russia. This character will award you with The strangers rifle.

During The Dark Beyond, she is spotted by the Guardian, looking down at them from the rocks that line the edge of the gorge where they are attempting to gain entrance to the Temple of Crota. During the Guardian's attempt to map the underground network of the Hive fortress on the Moon, the Exo Stranger contacted them from Venus' Northern Hemisphere in the Ishtar region. She tells the Guardian to meet her on Venus after they face the Hive in the Chamber of Night.

After the Guardian destroys the Chamber of Night, they meet the Exo Stranger on Venus after dispatching the Vex. She appeared after battle and commended the Guardian on their victory against the Vex, avoiding the question of why they were asked to meet her, stating she has no time.

entities.name: Eriana-3
entities.description:
Eriana-3 was a member of the ill-fated fireteam led by Eris Morn tasked with the assassination of Crota. She and everyone else in the fireteam died, leaving Eris as the only survivor. Eriana was also a Praxic Warlock and the owner of Eriana's Vow.

Eriana-3 was present during the initial attempt by Guardians to retake the Moon from the Hive. Knowing that the battle was going poorly, she captured and interrogated a Wizard, thus learning of Crota's existence. However, it would not reveal how to kill its master, much to her anger. It then showed her the death of Wei Ning and several other Guardians, further infuriating her.

In a moment of haste, she ordered all Guardians in the area to mount their Sparrows and ride to Mare Imbrium in hopes of turning the tide of the battle. After that particular battle ended in disaster, she went to a bar and stated how quiet it was without Wei's laugh. Eriana and Eris Morn decided to seek out Toland, The Shattered, seeking advice on how to kill Crota. Toland was recruited into their fireteam, along with the Hunters Omar Agah and Sai Mota, and the Titan Vell Tarlowe.

Eriana was in a romantic relationship with the Titan Wei Ning; they were introduced by the Hunter Pahanin in the Tower saloon. Wei's death is what sparked Eriana's quest for vengeance against Crota.

entities.description:
Felwinter, known by Rasputin as SIDHARRTA GOLEM, was a Warlock and one of the Iron Lords.

Felwinter started out as a warlord, with the Iron Lords coming to challenge him; he later abandoned the post and joined the Iron Lords himself after Timur recruited him in. He was known to be more brutal when compared to his other teammates; he was unwilling to show mercy, nor was he extremely bloodthirsty.

Felwinter was one of the nine Iron Lords who made it to the SIVA replication chamber and tried to stop the spread to adverse effects. He was killed when Jolder sealed the chamber with all the Iron Lords in it, bar Saladin, and blew it up.

The Guardian later came to the chamber, and using a discarded Iron Battle Axe, killed his Remnant, along with the Remnants of Gheleon and Jolder.

entities.name: Ahsa
entities.description:
Ahsa is a proto-Worm who resides on Titan after The Witness turned her family into Worm Gods by offering the power of the Sword Logic to them.

Ahsa was a proto-Worm who lived on Fundament until the Witness began to teach her family about the Sword and began to be seduced by the power it offers. Alongside her siblings Sel, Ora, and Leis, Ahsa fought against the Worm Gods Akka, Eir, Xol, Ur, Yul, and Xita. She eventually flees to Titan and finds refuge there. During the late Golden Age, a scientist named Gideon Tepon would learn of Ahsa's existence. She would attempt to warn the scientists of the Collapse brought on by the Black Fleet, but they ignore her warning. After the Collapse occurred, Ahsa would spend time alone on Titan until it was abducted by the Witness. She would observe a Guardian named Sloane as the latter was on a mission to pursue the Pyramid that was on the moon and send Sloane visions. Ahsa would later rescue Sloane after the latter became infused with Taken energies while she was investigating a Hive ritual used to summon the Black Terrace, the throne world of Xivu Arath. Sloane accepts the bond with Ahsa, and attempted to send a distress signal, which would be answered by the Vanguard after their attempt to follow the Witness into the Pale Heart have failed with Joxer's death and they have learned of a key to follow it from Soteria on Neptune. The Vanguard learns from Ahsa the origins of the Witness and the next step that will allow them to follow the Witness safely: the resurrection of Savathûn. The next step was handled by Ikora Rey and Eris Morn, who ascended into the Hive God of Vengeance by unintentionally invoking Ahsa in the ritual. She later gives up her Hive godhood after banishing Xivu Arath from her throne world and the Vanguard learned that the Ahamkara served as the solution they needed to follow the Witness safely.

Category:Worm Characters Category:Female Characters

Amanda Holliday was born to a couple of wandering scavengers outside the walls of the Last City. She became a skilled mechanic, working on the group's vehicles as they journeyed towards The City. Her mother, Nora, carried a shotgun called the Chaperone, which was later redesigned and made available to Guardians.

Amanda was present at the Red Legion's assault on The Last City, and flew The Guardian onto Ghaul's command ship.

Amanda was a hard-working, strong-willed person who appeared to get along well with most other residents of The Last City.

entities.name: Amtec
entities.description:
Amtec was a Cabal Psion Flayer that served in the Red Legion.

Being the youngest of the Psion Flayer sisters, her sisters were Ozletc, Tazaroc, and Niruul. She was described as beloved. Ozletc, Tazaroc, and Niruul would instruct Amtec to carry out their plan to enact vengeance should the gambit at the Sundial fail. After the sisters became Inotam and died soon after, Amtec began to carry out the instructions by drifting The Almighty in the direction of the The Last City. Zavala and Ana Bray would foil Amtec's plan by allowing the Guardian to power up Rasputin's Seraph Bunkers in the EDZ, the Moon, and Io. After the plans were foiled, a Psion conclave was formed by Yirix, who was intent on avenging the Psion Flayers at the Sundial and forming an independent Psion nation where the Psions would be united through the faith in the Y-goblet prior to the Cabal's conquest of the Psions.

Category:Psions Category:Female Characters
entities.short_description: Amtec was a Cabal Psion Flayer that served in the Red Legion.

entities.name: Anastasia Bray
entities.description:
Anastasia Bray, better known as Ana Bray, is a Hunter. She was present at the Battle of Twilight Gap where she wore a cloak with the same pattern as Strength of the Pack. She appears as a major supporting character in the Destiny 2 Warmind expansion as she attempts to uncover the mystery behind Rasputin and the polar ice caps of Mars.

Anastasia Bray is a member of House of Bray, she was told she was adopted when she was young to avoid telling her of her father's infidelity. She is one of the founders of the exoscience corporation Clovis Bray. Her whereabouts and exploits during the events of the Red War are largely unknown, with the exception of trace mentions by other characters or her redacted diary located in the Daito office in the Tower.

Anastasia Bray played a much larger role back before the events of Destiny, especially during the massive assault by the Fallen, known as the Battle of Twilight Gap, where the houses of Kings, Devils and Winter attacked the Last City all at once. She was in a fireteam with Lord Shaxx, Liu Feng, Nkechi-32, Idil Abdi and Truce during the battle. She engaged in a duel with a Fallen Archon but was thrown off the top of the wall and presumed dead for a long time.

Ana reappeared many years later and called upon the help of the Guardian in the beginning of the Destiny 2: Warmind expansion, bringing them to Mars, where she has decided to investigate her old life and heritage. She requested assistance after a frozen Hive army reawakened.

entities.name: Aunor Mahal
entities.description:
Functioning as a leader to the Praxic Order, Aunor takes it upon herself to monitor lighbearers for any signs of dark influence or corruption. This mission often puts her at odds with lightbearers such as The Drifter, who have no true allegiance to either Light or Dark. It was during her spying attempts on the Drifter that one of his acquaintances, an unnamed Guardian came under close scrutiny. Aunor sent encrypted messages to this Guardian in an attempt to turn them against the Drifter and to spy for her.

Over time, The Drifter became aware of Aunor's intentions, and attempted to expose her. The Drifter claims Aunor accidentally leveled a city block in a hostage rescue attempt. While this was still an unverified claim, it was enough to bring Aunor herself under enough scrutiny that she was forced to abandon efforts in terms of garnering support for her crusade against the Drifter and potential Dark Guardians. However, The Praxic Order still operates, keeping tabs on Guardians in the case of any falling to the darkness.

Despite her intentions being righteous, Aunor has had multiple people call her out for her corruption over the years. She has come under fire for having The Praxic Order function as spies rather than the passive Warlocks of old. While her monitoring comes across as hostile to those under her watch, Aunor still does not stray from her self-assigned purpose.

Sometime after the death of Cayde-6, the city's hunters had mostly vacated their dens within the The Last City. Aunor, seeing this as an opportunity to gain information from what remained behind, began raiding Hunter Dens. While searching a particular den, She came into contact with a Hunter named Ghost and a ghost named Tommy. Fearing punishment, the Hunter offered a bribe: His Exotic auto rifle, Tommy's Matchbook. Accepting, Aunor left the den and went on her way.

Ayane Takanome was the leader of a group known as Takanome's Rangers.

Ayane Takanome was the leader of the Rangers, one of the first groups that protected refugees traveling to The City. Despite not being a Guardian, she and her Rangers were often the only protection available in the early days of the Dark Age, when most Guardians were just starting to revive and regroup.

As their numbers dwindled and the Guardians took over, she and her group took to planting blue flowers along the safest routes, so as to guide refugees. A cloak similar to the one that she wore was later available for use by Hunter Guardians. While her story and that of her Rangers was later recounted by Chiyoko Mey, some believe Takanome and her group to be merely a myth.

She spawns Acolytes of Balwûr around the Court, which cannot be killed unless a Guardian is in a safe zone. On killing it, a temporary safe zone is created outside the underside of the platform. While Guardians are in that temporary safe zone, they can deal damage to Balwûr.

entities.description:
Efrideet is an Iron Lord and a Hunter. She served as the Iron Banner vendor in the Iron Temple.

Efrideet is well known for her strength; she once threw Saladin Forge at a Fallen Walker like a javelin. She was long thought to be dead until she returned, and she urges Guardians to participate in the Iron Banner as a way to strengthen their light.

The Vanguard was intrigued by Efrideet’s accounts of a nonmilitary Guardian community in the deep system, but Efrideet, though happy to talk about the group’s pacifist philosophies, refused to disclose the settlement’s location.

Efrideet was present fighting the Red Legion attack on the Last City and "Killed 216 Cabal with 199 bullets". Her fate is unknown, as the last sentence reads "I can't wait to see it. I'm coming home. Efrideet out."

entities.description:
Inotam, Oblivion's Triune was a Psion Flayer that formed from a joining ritual derived from ancient texts of the mind.

Inota was formed from the fusion of Ozletc, Tazaroc, and Niruul out of desperation for the Guardian interfering in the plans to undo the Vanguard's victory. Before fighting the Guardian within the Corridors of Time on Mercury, they would instruct Amtec to carry orders of vengeance should the elder sisters' gambit fail. The Guardian would fight Inotam and defeat them by killing the Psion Flayer sisters one by one, though it was not easy due to the Flayer's mastery over Void, Solar, and Arc. The death of Inotam would lead to the creation of a Psion conclave led by Yirix.

Jolder was one of nine Iron Lords who made it to the SIVA replication chamber. While in the chamber, SIVA infected her weapon and armor. Instead of escaping with Saladin, Jolder sealed herself, along with the remaining Iron Lords, inside the complex and detonated a remote charge, taking her life in the process.

The Guardian later killed her remnant in the chamber she sealed, along with the remnants of Felwinter and Gheleon.

Luzaku is an allied Hive Lightbearer who resides in The Blooming Deep sector within The Pale Heart.

Luzaku was an Acolyte when she died. She was raised by a Ghost named Euloch to become a Lightbearer Wizard loyal to the Lucent Brood. She became hesitant when Euloch encouraged her to crush an enemy Guardian's Ghost and was berated by her Ghost when she decided to give her enemy mercy. At some point, Luzaku would infiltrate a Black Fleet vessel and when the Witness entered the portal into the Pale Heart, was pulled into the Threshold. She began to ponder about the possibility of change from the Sky and decided to form a brood of her own where she would ally with the Coalition forces after they entered the Pale Heart. She eventually joins Caiatl, Mithrax, and the other Coalition forces in the final battle against The Witness.

entities.name: Navôta, Eir Spawn
entities.description:
Navôta, Eir Spawn is a boss in destiny 2

Navôta, Eir Spawn, is a powerful hive wizard that is introduced in the mission schism. Upon finding out she has killed Cas and Maeve, she is then defeated by the guardian. With her defeat the brood won't accept her back making her want to prove her worth. These events take place in the vanguard nightfall strike the disgraced.

Navôta in the nightfall strike the disgraced is the boss. At the very end the player will see a ritual circle at the bottom of the room where Navôta will appear. Navôta can shoot guardians with darkness if they are close enough. Navôta will summon many thrall and cursed thrall and if you are not able to kill her she will disappear and spawn a wave of knights, Adherents and 1 to 3 ogre. On

difficulties higher then adept one of the ogres will be a champion. When all hive have been eliminated Navôta will be spawned at the top of the broken bridge. When Navôta's health is at only one bar instead of disappearing she will teleport down to the bottom of the room and spawn even more hive. Once killed, the chest will be at the bottom area of the room in the center of the ritual circle.

entities.name: Niruul
entities.description:
Niruul, the Hollow Voice was a Psion Flayer that served in the Red Legion. She represented Void energy within the Psion Flayers.

Being the third-born of the Psion Flayer sisters, her sisters were Ozletc, Tazaroc, and Amtec. She was described as quiet. Ozletc, Tazaroc, and Niruul eventually discovered the Sundial, a device invented by Osiris to look for a timeline where Saint-14 could be saved, on Mercury. The sisters began to use the Sundial in an attempt to undo the Vanguard's victory over the Red War. After the sisters were defeated by the Guardian individually, they became desperate and would initiate a joining ritual derived from ancient texts of the mind. They would fuse into Inotam and instruct Amtec to carry out orders of vengeance should her older sisters fail in their gambit. Though the sisters were defeated in their fused form, another Psion named Yirix would form a Psion conclave to avenge the sisters.

Category:Cabal Ultras Category:Psions Category:Female Characters

entities.name: Omnigul
entities.description:
Omnigul, the Will of Crota was an ascendant Hive Wizard and boss of the The Will of Crota Strike in Old Russia. She returns in Shadowkeep as a Nightmare.

Omnigul was a disciple of Crota and attempted to assemble an army to awaken her master.

She is first encountered in Fist of Crota, fighting against the Fallen. After sustaining some damage, she will retreat. She then attempts to destroy Rasputin in Siege of the Warmind. She fights the Guardian, but after sustaining damage, retreats into a sealed off room and summons various Hive reinforcements to deal with the guardian, including the Might of Crota. However, these efforts prove futile as the Guardian defeats all the Hive, and Omnigul flees the area, ending the attack on Rasputin.

A Fireteam later tracks her down in the Jovian Complex, trying to restore what remains of her master's army, and kills her.

Ouros and the Sunbreakers were on Venus when the Vex attacked them. They escaped through a transfer gate to Mercury. A Guardian and their Ghost followed them.

On Mercury, Ouros greeted The Guardian and allowed them to test their Light in the forge. Upon acquiring the Hammer of Sol, Ouros allowed a horde of Vex to attack the Guardian to test their might. After the Guardian successfully defeated the Vex, Ouros congratulated the Guardian and welcomed them to the Sunbreakers.

Ouros and the rest of the Sunbreaker order were killed by the Red Legion during the Red War.

Perun was a Hunter and field commander of the Iron Lords. She was known for her skills as a strategist, and situational awareness that surpassed most Hunters.

Perun was a Hunter and wielded two rifles. Perun had participated in a battle with a rogue Lord named Segoth; Segoth had managed to headshot Radegast but she, Saladin, and Radegast fought on after multiple revivals, eventually causing Segoth to retreat.

Quinn Laghari is a Human living on Neomuna, a city on Neptune.

She earned 3 doctorates before she succeeded from her mentor Marco in becoming Neomuna's Chief Archivist, a role that is responsible for keeping up with the knowledge of the Golden Age as well as the history of Neptune. She chose to upload her consciousness into the CloudArk when the Shadow Legion began the siege of the city. She would observe Rohan's memorial and then tasks the Guardian with repairing Cloud Strider monuments that were damaged by the Vex. After the Cloud Strider monuments, she would uncover a message from Soteria regarding information on the next step that allow the Vanguard to follow The Witness through the portal to the Pale Heart. She would also give Guardians patrol missions throughout Neomuna.

entities.name: Safiyah
entities.description:
Safiyah was a Human who was the former wife of Zavala.

Safiyah was born in the Dark Age with her sister Amari and studied as a surgeon by studying Golden Age texts. While Zavala was the tutelage of Saladin Forge, Safiyah approached the gates and offered her services in exchange for shelter. She initially met Zavala with detestation, but she later came to respect him over time. She and Zavala later adopted Hakim after an Eliksni raid forced the child to be orphaned. She continued to stay with Zavala as he trained Hakim to fight. By the time Hakim had reached the age of 17, another raid occurred led by the House of Devils, but this time Hakim died saving Zavala from Kethiks. She became stricken with grief and would part ways with Zavala, eventually having a daughter before her death. As the Leviathan was infested Egregore and Calus began to commune with the Lunar Pyramid, Zavala became tormented by the Nightmare of Safiyah until he was able to let go of his grief. The Witness later exploits Zavala's grief in the attempt to lure him away from his faith in The Traveler. He eventually moves on from his grief after the Witness kills his Ghost, Targe.

entities.name: Sloane
entities.description:
Sloane was a Titan of The Last City who served as a Vanguard scout. During the events of the Red War, Sloane served as Commander Zavala's deputy and secured the moon Titan as an outpost for the Vanguard. She was last seen attacking a Pyramid Ship on Titan.

Sloane first contacted the Guardian and their Ghost when they arrived in orbit around Titan after leaving The Farm. She served as a voice of reason between the Guardian and Commander Zavala, who was still shaken by the loss of the City. Sloane informed the Guardian of the tasks at hand: get the station operational, prepare the Guardian fleet, decrypt Red Legion transmissions, and ultimately plan a counteroffensive.

Initially, Sloane tasked the Guardian with clearing out the command center. Once that was done, she guided them through the chore of getting the power back online, along with Zavala and Amanda Holliday. Needing a Golden Age CPU to crack some high-priority Red Legion communiques, she next instructed them to the Arcology, an area infested with Hive. Upon recovering the computer system, Sloane then informed the gathered Guardians of the threat posed by the Cabal superweapon The Almighty. She felt the situation to be hopeless, but Zavala disagreed.

At one point, she briefed a group of rather cocky Guardians who were preparing to undertake a mission against the Hive. In addition, Sloane relayed the last transmission before the Sunbreakers were overrun and destroyed, as well as reports of the Fallen abandoning the Cosmodrome.

She became the teacher of the royal offspring of the Osmium Court, a floating continent on the gas giant Fundament. When the Osmium king's mind began to crumble from senility and madness, Taox realized his death was imminent, and feared that all of his daughters were too wayward and weak to ascend the Osmium Throne and rule effectively. Using her trusted position, she secretly invited the rival Helium Drinkers of the Helium Court to invade the Osmium Court, assassinate the royal family, and make her regent of the continent under the Helium king.

entities.name: Tazaroc
entities.description:
Tazaroc, the Sun Eater was a Psion Flayer that served in the Red Legion. She represented Solar energy within the Psion Flayers.

Being the second-born of the Psion Flayer sisters, her sisters were Ozletc, Niruul, and Amtec. She was described as impatient. Ozletc, Tazaroc, and Niruul eventually discovered the Sundial, a device invented by Osiris to look for a timeline where Saint-14 could be saved, on Mercury. The sisters began to use the Sundial in an attempt to undo the Vanguard's victory over the Red War. After the sisters were defeated by the Guardian individually, they became desperate and would initiate a joining ritual derived from ancient texts of the mind. They would fuse into Inotam and instruct Amtec to carry out orders of vengeance should her older sisters fail in their gambit. Though the sisters were defeated in their fused form, another Psion named Yirix would form a Psion conclave to avenge the sisters.

Yaviks wishes to see the hierarchy of the Fallen replaced by the hierarchy of The Reef, which caters to anarchism and power given to those who claim it themselves. She is responsible for the destruction of eight major Awoken outposts, six Techeun temples, and has taken hundreds of lives.

Yaviks is the target of the activity Target: The Rider.

entities.name: Yirix
entities.description:
Yirix was a Psion that served in the Red Legion before forming a Psion conclave with the mission to create a unified Psion through the pre-Cabal faith of the Y-goblet and vengeance of the Psion Flayers at the Sundial.

She originally was onboard the Glykon Volatus where friend Qinziq was requesting the research vessel to be under Calus's control. Before leaving, she witnesses Qinziq traveling along with Katabasis and Bahr'Toran. Later, after the death of Ozletc, Tazaroc, and Niruul as well as the destruction of The Almighty at Rasputin's hands, Yirix formed the Psion conclave to carry out Amtec's order to avenge her elder sisters by assassinating the Vanguard Commander Zavala using Ixel's intel. Her conclave began to strike as the Vanguard were engaging in the Rites of Proving with Caiatl's Imperial Cabal. The conclave would strike again as the Vanguard were signing an armistice with Caiatl after the Guardian defeated Ignovun, sending in Qalec and Valir. After the assassination attempts on Zavala failed and Mars returned to the Sol System, Yirix would create a Psionic propaganda to integrate her forces with Calus and The Witness. After the Witness was defeated by The Coalition and the Echoes were created, Yirix began to assume command of Shadow Legion and some Dread forces and send her forces to search for the Echo claimed by Maya Sundaresh.

entities.description:
Fynch is a Hive Ghost who betrayed his Lightbearer once he saw Savathûn's plans after she became a Lightbearer and formed the Lucent Brood

Fynch did find his Hive Lightbearer, but he defected once he saw how the Hive were using The Light. He became a critical ally in the Vanguard's plan to confront Savathûn after she posed as Osiris and she was escape the exorcism ritual at the cost of her worm being extracted. He contacted the Guardian when they were tasked by Ikora Rey to gain clues on how Savathûn acquired the Light. He would meet them once they dealt with the Scorn that were invading the throne world. He would have them recover the following items of interest throughout the throne world: Sagira's Ghost shell, a fragment of the Tablets of Ruin, and the calcified worm familiar, and each one of them was was recovered from the temples dedicated to a Hive god. After Savathûn was defeated, he and Ikora tasked the Guardian with securing the Wellspring from the Lucent Brood and Scorn. It is soon revealed that the Scorn were sent in by a powerful wielder of Darkness, who was later revealed to be Rhulk, to counter the Light from the Wellspring that was stored by Savathûn. He later congratulated them on Rhulk's death.

entities.name: Immaru
entities.description:
Immaru is a Hive Ghost who resurrected Savathûn following the exorcism ritual and is the de facto leader of the Lucent Brood in Savathûn's absence.

Immaru was a Ghost who harbored hatred for Guardians' usage of the Light and became fascinated with the Sword Logic. He would be the first Ghost to resurrect a Hive member, namely Savathûn, into the Light. He taught Savathûn how to wield the Light's power before the Guardian made their way into the High Coven. The Guardian first met Immaru once Savathûn and subsequently disappeared after The Traveler returned to The Last City. Since her defeat, he became the leader of the Lucent Brood and issued commands to them through the Hive Ghost network. He even tasked his forces with stealing the Osmium fragment that was later used to create the Edge of Action, Edge of Intent, and Edge of Concurrence.

Later, when Ahsa revealed to the Vanguard that the next step to follow The Witness through The Pale Heart portal required Savathûn to be brought back, he refused to bring her back until Xivu Arath. He began expressing doubts about Eris Morn's plan to gain enough tithes to challenge Xivu Arath once she ascended into the Hive God of Vengeance. Eris improvised on her plan when she realizes that she doesn’t have enough tributes to challenge Xivu Arath, so she had Immaru resurrect Savathûn anyway. He realizes that Eris would instead use the tithes to banish Xivu Arath from the Black Terrace, her throne World. entities.name: Dredgen Yor
entities.description:
Rezyl Azzir was resurrected during the Dark Age by his Ghost, and made his way to a refugee camp located beneath the Traveler. At this time many worshiped the Traveler as a god, and formed Factions amongst themselves. Many of the Risen chose to join factions as warlords and enforcers, sowing chaos and distrust. Rezyl and others soon saw that the factions were a threat to the survival of Humanity, and the Risen who joined them were misusing their Light. Due to this dispute, the Faction Wars erupted and fighting quickly spread.

The war ended when the Fallen arrived and began attacking the refugees. Rezyl became a champion of both conflicts as he broke the power of the factions and helped to repel the Fallen assault. Many turned to him as a hero, and some believing that he may even be a god. With the factions now defeated, the camp became united and formed the Last City, and built walls to protect themselves. Over time more survivors and Risen arrived, and they soon became known as Guardians, who swore to protect Humanity. For years he watched the City grow and new Guardians rise, but grew fearful of old stories that told of servants of the Darkness coming to finish what was started during the Collapse. At the end of each day Rezyl would stare up at the Moon wondering what threat lurked up there.

Rezyl was corrupted by the Hive and was eventually killed by Shin Malphur.

He had a foul-smelling den in an unknown location, with memorabilia from his various operations, including but not limited to Ahamkara bones, coyote skeletons, and mastodon skulls. He is shown to be extremely good with knives when he flips Swiftling and throws it, shattering a Fallen shin bone.

He was one of nine Iron Lords who made it to the SIVA replication chamber, and tried to curb the spread of SIVA to adverse effects. Gheleon was killed when Jolder sealed the chamber with all Iron Lords inside, bar Saladin, and blew it up.

A Guardian later came to the chamber and killed his Remnant, along with the Remnants of Felwinter and Jolder.

entities.name: Jaren Ward
entities.description:
Jaren Ward was a Hunter who lived during the Dark Age and was the original owner of the Last Word. He was the father figure of Shin Malphur until his death at the hands of Dredgen Yor.

At one point, Jaren Ward visited the settlement of Palamon, outside the walls of the Last City. There he met Shin Malphur, who would later describe him as "a light" and his third father figure of sorts. The entire town turned out to greet him, but young Shin was more excited and curious than most. At that point, Jaren offered his hand cannon to him.

At one point after the destruction of Palamon, Jaren, Shin, and seven others set out to track down Dredgen Yor. They tracked him for at least a week without a sign of their quarry, but then disaster struck. Three members of their party were killed, and Jaren left the group. In the night, they heard the familiar gunshots of The Last Word, followed by a single shot from another gun. After Jaren's death, his Ghost returned and scanned Shin, then spoke to him.

Both Shaxx and Zavala were his students, but his relationship with Shaxx became strained following the battle. the other being Efrideet.

Shaxx is a hero of the Battle of Twilight Gap and led a counterattack against the Fallen that pushed them from The Last City's walls, along with Nkechi-32, Idil Abdi, Truce, Liu Feng and Ana Bray.

He and Zavala were both proteges of Lord Saladin, however Shaxx's relationship with Saladin has become strained since the Battle of Twilight Gap. He is still on good terms with Zavala.

Shaxx now serves as the head of the Crucible in the City. At one point, executives from Tex Mechanica tried to bribe Shaxx into rigging Crucible matches in order to make their weapons look good. Shaxx refused, referring to their equipment as "junk."

Shin was raised in the settlement of Palamon, one of the last human outposts outside the City, which was led by Magistrate Loken. When Shin was very young, his parents were taken by Dregs. Shin was then taken in by another resident of Palamon, who would raise Shin as his foster father.

After Jaren was killed by Dredgen Yor, Jaren's Ghost talked with Shin.

Shin is someone who seeks justice, sometimes even when it is not wise to do so.

Believing there would be others, they created a group known as the Shadows of Yor, claiming that his horrible deeds were all a lie created to frame him as evil. entities.name: Toland, the Shattered
entities.description:
Toland, the Shattered was a Warlock that was exiled from The Last City due to his obsession with the Hive. He joined the fireteam that attempted to kill Crota, Son of Oryx. He, along with every other Guardian on the team save for Eris Morn, was killed by the Hive.

At some point, he had been exiled for having been thought to have gone mad, due to his ramblings about the Hive. Later, Toland was recruited into a fireteam with Eris Morn during an attempt on Crota's life. He was already quite old by Guardian standards at this time.

While he failed to kill Crota, he did manage to pass on some of his knowledge of the Hive to Eris before his death. With this, she was able to save a Guardian's life when a mission to steal part of Crota's soul went awry. Toland gave the "Emerald Light" bond to Eris so the Hive would think that she was one of them.

In Destiny 2, Toland can be found in the Ascendant Plane, although he spawns in a different place sometimes. The player will also need the Tincture of Queensfoil to find him.

When the Guardian was close to killing him, Oryx recruited Baxx into the Taken. After the Guardian stole the shard, Baxx was teleported back as a Taken Ogre under the name of Baxx, Hand of Oryx.

Later, when the Guardian attempted to gather some of Crota's death essence into that shard, Baxx appeared along with Ta'aun, Hand of Oryx and attacked the Guardian. They were unsuccessful, and the Guardian escaped again.

When the Guardian entered the Ascendant Realm on the Dreadnaught intending to kill Oryx, Baxx once again appeared with Ta'aun and attacked the Guardian. Both Baxx and Ta'aun were killed by the Guardian.

The High Celebrant was sent to the Solar System after the disappearance of Io, Titan, Mars, and Mercury. Tasked with the mission of preparing for Xivu Arath's arrival with the Cryptoliths planted on the Moon, the Dreaming City, and the Tangled Shore. The Celebrant encountered Osiris on the moon, and proceded to kill Osiris' Ghost Sagira, making Osiris mortal.

During the final mission during Season of the Hunt, Coup de Grâce, the Guardian and Crow located the High Celebrant and used the lure to bring it to the Cryptolith in the Dreaming City. After a chase, the High Celebrant was trapped by Crow, who prevented the High Celebrant from escaping from the Ascendant Plane by blocking their portal, allowing the Guardian to defeat the Celebrant within the Ascendant Plane, making their death permanent.

When summoned, a Servile Ogre spawns with Kagoor, with Kagoor protected with a shield impervious to any forms of attack; the shield will go down when the Servile Ogre is killed. The Servile Ogre has the same attacks as a normal Ogre, however it is much stronger and much harder to take down with normal gunfire.

Around the Court of Oryx, Kagoor will spawn special variants of Acolyte's Eyes, known as Maleficent Eyes. Killing a Maleficent Eye will grant the Guardian who killed it a buff known as "Ogre's Fury", which greatly increases damage dealt against the Servile Ogre; this buff can stack up to three times and lasts approximately thirty seconds. Once the Servile Ogre is dead, Kagoor is completely vulnerable to any form of attack and must be killed while vulnerable; if not killed during that time, another Servile Ogre spawns, and Kagoor's shield will regenerate instantly, rendering her impervious to any form of attack again.

He led both Hive and Taken Knights into Bunker RAS-2 to achieve this goal. In his attempt, he was killed by a Guardian who was investigating a strange signal sent by Rasputin.

Kelgorath, Risen from Bones was a servant of Xivu Arath. He was sent by Xivu Arath to stop the Guardian from rescuing the lost Techeuns from the Ley Lines.

Kelgorath was a member of the Hidden Swarm before he denounced the actions of Savathûn since the Black Fleet caused the planetary bodies to disappear. He eventually pledges his allegiance to Xivu Arath once her High Celebrant decapitated Osiris and his Ghost, Sagira. After pledging his allegiance to Xivu Arath fully, he found purpose and would be deployed to the Dreaming City as the Guardian, Saint-14, and Crow pursue Savathûn, who at the time was under the guise of Osiris. After being slayed by the Guardian, he eventually returns in an attempt to steal Ager's Scepter. He fails to steal the weapon and was returned again. He was deployed to the Dreaming City once more to stop the ritual to separate Savathûn from her Worm. He was defeated and then risen again as a Darkblade. After Mars returned to the system and the Witch Queen was defeated by the Guardian, Xivu Arath orders Kelgorath to occupy Mars and claim the Warsat network. After suffering yet another defeat by the Guardian, he later became Taken from Bones and would be ordered to stop the Guardian on Titan from recovering the egregore corals to strengthen the connection between Sloane and Ahsa. He fails once more.

entities.name: Nokris
entities.description:
Nokris was born shortly after Crota, and was disfavored by his father, Oryx, due to his physical weakness. Fortunately for Nokris, what he lacked in strength, he made up for in intellect.

In an attempt to prove himself to his father, Nokris made a plea to the Worm Gods in an attempt to gain the same power Oryx once gained from them. The Worm Gods all rejected Nokris, save for Xol, the weakest of the Worms. Nokris pledged his loyalty and service to the worm in exchange for knowledge of the Deep, as well as the power of necromancy. This enraged Oryx, as reviving the dead went directly against the Sword Logic. As a result, Oryx banished Nokris and his followers, and removed any mention of his son, except for a statue in the Dreadnaught.

After Nokris was exiled by his father, he traveled to Mars and was imprisoned, along with Xol, by the Warmind Rasputin shortly after their arrival. Nokris and Xol eventually both escaped and began to take over Mars in the hopes of finally destroying Rasputin. However, the Guardian stopped Nokris before he could carry out his plans.

After the deaths of Nokris and Xol, Nokris was able to escape death through the use of his Necromancy. Savathûn took notice and decided to take up a bargain with him. In exchange for teaching her his Necromancy, Nokris would learn to Take, and be bounded to Savathûn. During the Interference missions, he speaks to the Guardian and the Ghost as Savathûn and he attempt to halt the communications between the Darkness and the Guardian.

entities.name: Osmium King
entities.description:
The Osmium King was a proto-Hive (krill) who ruled the continent called the Osmium Court on the gas giant planet Fundament. He had three surviving daughters: Xi Ro, Sathona, and Aurash.

By the time the Osmium King had reached ten years of age, a lifetime for the short-lived proto-Hive species, he had become senile and insane. In his madness, he locked himself in the Royal Orrery and obsessed over the orbits of Fundament's 52 moons.

Taox, a sterile Mother and the teacher of the royal offspring, knew the Osmium King's death was imminent, but feared that all of his daughters were too wayward and weak to ascend to the Osmium Throne and rule effectively. Secretly, she invited the rival Helium Drinkers of the Helium Court to invade the Osmium Court, assassinate the royal family, and make her regent of the continent under Helium King.

Hashladûn, Besurith, Kinox, and Voshir would view his ascension as a threat to their scheme. Zulmak would be killed by Azavath while her body was possessed by Akrazul, in a total violation of the Sword Logic; however, his essence was used by the Daughters of Crota when the Lunar Pyramid was uncovered by Eris Morn. He was made into a hybrid of Hive infused with Nightmare energy and the remaining daughters would use a ritual to empower him. entities.name: Clovis Bray I
entities.description:
Clovis Bray I was a Golden Age scientist, the patriarch of the Bray family, and the founder of the technology and research company Clovis Bray.

At some point during the Golden Age or before, Clovis I founded the Clovis Bray exoscience corporation. He was married to Lusia Lin. His son, Clovis Bray II, became a senior researcher at the company, as did his grandchildren Elisabeth, Alton, Wilhelmina and Anastasia.

Toward the end of his life, Bray embarked on a mission to Europa, both to catalogue the moon's native life-forms and to investigate a source of power alluded to in messages from the K1 anomaly. The paracausal force empowering the artifact, which Bray referred to as "Clarity", had promised Bray the secret to immortality - a secret which Bray was desperate to obtain.

Upon reaching Europa, Bray discovered both native life in the moon's subsurface ocean, and the source of "Clarity," which Bray named "Clarity Control". Bray requested that his granddaughter Elisabeth, who was suffering from inherited fatal insomnia caused by the elder Bray's genetic meddling, join him and assist with his work, which she agreed to do.

entities.name: Drifter
entities.description:
Drifter is a rogue Guardian and the host of Gambit. He serves as a vendor in the Tower. During Gambit matches, he appears in his ship, the Derelict, to spectate and determine the horde of enemies the Guardians must face.

Drifter was resurrected by a Ghost during the Dark Ages. He starved to death at least once out in the wild. It appears that his first chosen name was Germaine, which he went by while living in a village called Eaton. While living there, he hid his Light and secretly helped the village to be kept fed. He would send out his Ghost to search for food up to 100 leagues away. Occasionally he would also babysit a child in the village, Yu, when Judson, her family's neighbor, was being a little too aggressive and hostile.

Judson was a friend of the Drifter, and was a very good huntsman. Eventually while the Drifter lived in Eaton, a group of Iron Lords, led by Lord Dryden, payed the people of the village several months worth of food and supplies so that they could stay a week to stake out a Warlord named the Red Man. The village accepted the bargain, and Judson who highly disagreed, decided to leave the village that night.

The Red Man assumed that a lone Ghost he had seen was Judson's, when it actually was the Drifter's Ghost. The Red Man and five other Warlords brought Judson back to Eaton a week later at midday, the Red Man questioning the villagers, asking where the Iron Lord's were, now assuming the Ghost belonged to one of them. The Drifter responded, saying that the villagers payed the Iron Lords for food and supplies, and then the Iron Lords left. The Red Man, not believing, shot Yu's father. Shortly after, Judson grabbed a Fallen shock blade and attacked the War Lords, until one of them grabbed the spear, stabbed him in the side with a blade and flung him.

He served as the news anchor for Neomuna Civil News. He would periodically make news announcements to the citizens of Neomuna during the Shadow Legion's city. He eventually would regularly interview with various characters as the Guardian seemed to understand the nature of Strand, defeat Calus, and find a way through the portal that The Witness opened into the Pale Heart, including Osiris, Caiatl, and Nimbus. After the Guardian learned that the Ahamkara were the only solution to the Witness and it responded to Crow being chosen to be the first Guardian to enter the Pale Heart, Jisu would be the featured guest of an interview from Emmanuil Utkin of the City Herald.

entities.name: Lodi
entities.description:
Lodi, known by his government name as Louis Yero is a Human from the Space Age who eventually became the latest Emissary of The Nine, succeeding Xûr and Orin.

Born in Lodi, Wisconsin where his nickname "Lodi" came from, Louis Yero became a polyglot who would employ at the Department of External Observation, a United States agency tasked with investigating extraterrestrial anomalies throughout Earth and has an office based in Chicago, Illinois. At the time he began employing there, the DEO was investigating an unknown energy weapon linked to John F. Kennedy's assassination. During his time there, he met a colleague who was a mathematician working on Project Graviton, Dr. Nella Davis. After she was killed by a train sent forward in time by the Nine, Louis would answer a phone inside and was also pulled forward in time into the City Age following The Witness's death and the creation of the Echoes. He arrived on Kepler after Orin left her position as the Emissary of the Nine and would fall into the care of the AION Initiative, a scientific group in Kepler who once worked alongside the House of Exile before the latter began to worship a being known to them as "the Giver". He adopted his nickname upon meeting with the AION Initiative and began recording a series of messages, one of them being received from the Anomaly near Vesper Station on Europa's orbit by Astraea, the central AI aboard there. The Guardian, the Drifter, and Ikora Rey met Lodi as the Vanguard was investigating a singularity that is threatening the planetoid. He later began receiving strange visions and was in the process of becoming the next Emissary of the Nine under the guidance of Orin, who he met later on. When he later learned that the Nine can only send objects forwards in time and not backwards, as well as the Collapse, Lodi expressed his frustration at the decimation of human civilization nor exactly how far in the future he was. Lodi revealed to Ikora that he recognized her because she resembled his colleague during his time at the DEO. He was able to embrace his role as the Emissary when he learned that the Nine member III was killed by the Conductor by forcing it, a 4-dimensional being, into a 3-dimensional space and tasked the Guardian recovering an asset from Project Graviton, which was later found to be Graviton Spike.

entities.name: Nimbus
entities.description:
Nimbus, formerly Dara Danu is Neomuna's sole and current Cloud Strider. They took over the position from their former mentor, Rohan, when he sacrificed himself to destroy the Radial Mast.

Nimbus was known by the Human name of Dara Danu prior to the death of Rohan's mentor, Tramotane. Dara was selected to take up the mantle of Cloud Strider after undergoing the augmentations within the Sidereal and selected Nimbus as their Cloud Strider callsign.

Nimbus and Rohan would meet the Guardian after The Witness instructed Calus and his Shadow Legion forces to find the Veil. As the Guardian continue the mission to stop Calus from claiming the Veil, Nimbus would assist the Guardian and Osirisin the mastery over Strand. They would become the sole Cloud Strider after Rohan sacrificed himself to destroy the Radial Mast. They, along with Caiatl, Osiris, and the Guardian, would prepare for Calus to assault the Veil Containment facility with arming Neomuna's defense systems. Despite their defense, Calus was able to blast open the facility, forcing the Guardian. While exploring the Veil Containment facility, Nimbus explains that the Ishtar Collective technology within the facility was used as a CloudArk prototype. Nimbus later catches up with the Guardian as the Witness uses Ghost to create the link it needed to enter the Traveler's Pale Heart.

Despite the loss, the Guardian and Osiris would help Nimbus track down Rohan's notes after the memorial was conducted within the Hall of Heroes, in the attempt to learn more about the Veil and its connection with the portal. Rohan's notes lead into the Black Garden with Nimbus pressing on against Osiris's recommendation. Nimbus eventually concedes upon finding Rohan’s lost weapon and Osiris reminding them of their duty as a Cloud Strider. After recovering data from the Conceptual Mind, they learn that the Black Heart was an incomplete copy of the Veil constructed by the Sol Divisive. After the data was handed over to Nimbus, they would return to the Veil Containment facility and uncover the truth from audio logs left behind by Chioma Esi.
entities.short_description: Nimbus, formerly Dara Danu is Neomuna's sole and current Cloud Strider. They took over the position from their former mentor, Rohan, when he sacrificed himself to destroy the Radial Mast.

entities.name: Rohan
entities.description:
Rohan was a former Cloud Strider who mentioned Nimbus after the death of his mentor, Tramotane.

After the death of Tramotane's mentor, Rohan became the next Cloud Strider to defend Neomuna. At one point during his training, Rohan used the CloudArk to gain access to the Black Garden. While in the Black Garden, he witnessed the creation of the Black Heart, a false replica of the Veil created by the Sol Divisive Vex at the behest of The Witness. He would report the Black Heart's creation to the Neomuna Council, but they didn’t view it as a threat to Neomuna's survival. After the death of Tramotane, he selected Nimbus, who at the time went by the Human name of Dara Danu, to become the next Cloud Strider. Him and Nimbus eventually meet with the Guardian and Osiris when the Shadow Legion began their siege of the city. After the Guardian infiltrated the Typhon Imperator and failed the destroy the Radial Mast, Rohan would instruct them to restore power to the CloudArk. They were successful in spite of the Shadow Legion’s attempt to ambush them in the escape. Rohan would formulate the next move as the Shadow Legion began transporting the Radial Mast into the city. He would eventually sacrifice himself to destroy the Radial Mast, and his memorial was later held in the Hall of Heroes by Quinn Laghari. His notes of the Black Garden would be useful in attempting to learn more about the Veil when the Witness used its link to enter the Pale Heart.

entities.description:
The Iron Lords were a group of legendary Guardians established before the rise of The Last City and the creation of the Vanguard. They were renowned for their patrols around the City during the Battle of Six Fronts and the building of the Wall.

The Iron Lords had a fortress located on Felwinter Peak which was used as their primary stronghold in Old Russia. Over a hundred years ago, many Iron Lords sacrificed their lives in the battle with Rasputin to claim an ancient technology called SIVA, and the subsequent battle to contain it after it proved to be a significant threat to humanity. Out of the hundreds that went into what would later be named the Plaguelands, only nine Lords made it to the SIVA replication chamber. The nine tried to end the SIVA threat to adverse effects, as SIVA began to infect their weapons and armor, taking their lives in the process. Lord Saladin was long thought to be the only Iron Lord to have survived against the SIVA virus until Efrideet was discovered to be alive when she appeared as an Iron Banner vendor in the Iron Temple.

Within the ranks of the Iron Lords, a famous unit known as the Iron Wolves also existed. While its unknown why they had such renown, it is known that they too fell during the battle with SIVA.

entities.description:

The Speaker is located in Tower North and sells a variety of legendary class items and emblems for Motes of Light. With the release of The Taken King, he also sells a variety of Ghost shells. He was murdered by The Consul during the Red War.

The Speaker was captured during the Red Legion's attack on The City. After this, he was interrogated by Ghaul about how to get Light from the Traveler. When The Guardian and the Vanguard fought to recapture The City from the Red Legion, The Speaker was released from his restraints by The Consul and died.

The Speaker also sell a variety of Ghost Shells for 180 Glimmer each. Each Ghost Shell is set at level 34, 36, and 38 and each one is capped at 190 light.

Xûr is a strange being who occasionally appears from time to time, selling strange weapons and armor to Guardians. He serves the enigmatic entities known as The Nine.

Xûr was a mysterious merchant who began appearing in the Sol System after the end of the Great Ahamkara Hunt, when the Vanguard drove the Ahamkara to extinction with Riven and Taranis being the species' last living survivors. Xûr was selected by the Nine as their first Emissary, where the Nine wished to understand Guardians. Xûr was confronted by an Awoken Guardian named Orin, the future second Emissary of the Nine, as she was investigating Sjur Eido's death at Mara Sov's request and injured him severely that he is hunched over permanently. Later, Xûr released Skolas from the Prison of Elders at the behest of the Nine, instigating the House of Wolves' rebellion against the Awoken. He then hosted the Dares of Eternity alongside his equine companion Starhorse. A Hidden report from Aunor Mahal revealed that a rogue Cabal faction was able to acquire weaponry and flight telemetry from Xûr whilst the Guardian and Ikora Rey investigated Kepler and met Lodi, who became the latest Emissary of the Nine after Orin left that position.

In Destiny, Xûr is a vendor who sells exotic weapons, exotic armor, engrams, Exotic Shards, and consumables in exchange for Strange Coins and Motes of Light. He appears in different locations in the Tower and Vestian Outpost every weekend from 9:00 AM Friday to 9:00 AM Sunday UTC. The Agent of the Nine disappears every Sunday and won’t return until next Friday.

entities.name: Kaliks Reborn
entities.description:
Kaliks Reborn is an ultra Servitor from the House of Wolves. It is the final boss of the Prison of Elders challenge Machine Wrath.

Kaliks Reborn was built from the parts of lesser Servitors. The Fallen that serve it are so loyal to the lost Kaliks Prime that they willingly give all their ether to fuel the prime servitor. It is seen by its followers as the resurrection of Kaliks Prime. With Kaliks, the House of Wolves may gain new strength, or a new house may rise.

During the fight, Kaliks Reborn behaves like a normal Servitor, firing its Void eye blast and teleporting around the arena. It will actively pursue players around the arena to line up shots with its main weapon. When Kaliks Reborn has lost 25% of its health, a message will appear: "Kaliks summons his archons." At this point, a group of Dreg Majors will be summoned, named Archon Servants. Archon Servants are very resilient to damage and can kill a Guardian quickly. After approximately 30 seconds, another message will appear: "Kaliks Reborn gorges on ether." Any Archon Servants still alive will be sacrificed to Kaliks, and in doing so, he will regain health. This repeats when Kaliks have lost 50% and 75% of its health. At 50%, a Reaver Captain will spawn alongside the Archon Servants. If this Captain is not killed before it reaches its destination, the round will restart.
